purpose: Record the prerequisites and explicit blockers for any future aggregation or recommendation step after per-dimension comparison.
criticalDistinctions: Theme Adapter status=resolved means its provider-requirement plan is resolved; it does not mean requested dimension assessments are resolved.
providerRequirements are requests for evidence/assessment providers, not DimensionAssessment outputs.
dimensionEvidence being empty must never be treated as neutral, adverse, or zero score.
Explicit user preference capture is not an aggregation formula.

requirements: Every requested dimension for every in-scope alternative has a normalized DimensionAssessment or an explicit not_applicable state.
Every dimension that participates in ordering has an active reviewed Domain Comparator.
Comparator compatibility has been established for the exact semanticMeaning and contractFamily used by both alternatives.
All hard constraints have explicit provider results; missing constraints are not treated as satisfied.
User preference policy is explicit for any aggregation that depends on priorities.
An aggregation policy has been independently researched, reviewed and versioned.
The aggregation policy defines mixed, tied, partial and incomparable dimension behavior without hidden numeric scoring.
High-stakes factual dimensions such as legal exposure are supplied by appropriate modern factual providers rather than divination inference.
Regression covers contradictory dimensions, missing dimensions, hard-constraint failure, ties, partial alternatives and incomparable dimensions.
Calibration or sealed evaluation passes before any recommendation becomes current.
Current-22 behavior remains unchanged unless a separate migration is approved.

allowedOutputsV01: normalized dimension assessment records when available
per-dimension relation only when a registered comparator exists
hard-constraint unresolved/satisfied/violated state when supplied by the responsible provider

researchCandidatesNotRules.note: Could only be studied when the user explicitly ranks dimensions and every preceding priority dimension has a reviewed comparator.
Could only be studied when hard constraints are evaluated by responsible factual/domain providers and failure semantics are reviewed.
Cannot be used until all participating dimensions have registered comparators and partial/incomparable behavior is defined.
